data.cultural_impact: The name Firouz has a rich cultural history, especially in Persian and Islamic traditions. In Persian folklore, Firouz is a legendary hero and king known for his lion-like bravery and strength. He is revered for his valor and reign over ancient Persia. This name has also been popularized in various Islamic cultures, where it has become a symbol of power, leadership, and victory. In some Arab regions, it is customary to give this name to boys born during prosperous and victorious times.

He was responsible for the construction of the magnificent Abbasid Palace in Baghdad and the establishment of the House of Wisdom, which became a leading center for the translation of Greek and other foreign works into Arabic.

historical_references.reference: Firouz Shah Tughlak, also known as Muhammad ibn Tughluq, was the sultan of the Tughluq Empire in India from 1325 to 1351 AD. He is best known for his extensive territorial expansion, which extended the Tughluq Empire from northern India to the Deccan in the south. The size of his empire and his centralized bureaucracy made it difficult to govern effectively, and his policies led to widespread famine and social unrest.
